title: Cost to Have Cards Graded (2026)
verdict: The cost to have cards graded in 2026 is a flat $18 a card at AGS, compared with $24.99 to $79.99 on PSA's listed value tiers.

The fee is only part of the bill. Add shipping both ways, insurance and supplies, and at some graders a membership or a value upcharge. The table below uses each company's own listed prices as of November 18, 2026.

why: One price covers everything. $18 buys the scan, the grade, eight subgrades, the report and the slab, for any card at any value. Orders of 30 or more TCG cards pay $15 a card on the standard bulk tier.

The terms are easy. There is no minimum submission, no membership and no contract, and AGS does not charge until the cards are graded and ready to ship. New customers get 20% off a first order with code AGSNEW20.
Thirty cards gets you the bulk rate. The report, the subgrades and the slab are the same as on a single-card order, so a shop can list every card with its scan attached.

faq.q: What is the cost to have cards graded?
faq.a: Most entry tiers cost $10 to $50 a card in November 2026. AGS is $18 with subgrades and a report included.

faq.q: Is there a discount on a first AGS order?
faq.a: Yes. AGS lists code AGSNEW20 for 20% off a first grading order.

faq.q: What costs come on top of the grading fee?
faq.a: Shipping to the grader, return shipping and insurance, and supplies such as penny sleeves and card savers. Some graders add membership fees, subgrade fees or value upcharges. AGS adds return shipping at checkout.

faq.q: How much does AGS charge to grade a card?
faq.a: $18 per card at the standard rate, whatever the card is worth. Bulk orders of 30 or more TCG cards are $15 each at 20 business days, $20 at 10 or $30 at 5. Sports and non-TCG bulk is $3 more per tier.

faq.q: Is there a minimum number of cards?
faq.a: Not at AGS. You can send one card at $18, and bulk pricing needs 30. CGC's bulk tier needs 10 cards, ISA needs 10, and GMA needs 10 to 25 depending on the tier.
